nodes.label: Claude Code interactive workflow
nodes.rationale: Passes no prompt input, so the action stays in interactive mode and waits to be mentioned rather than running unprompted.

nodes.label: sender.type != Bot guard
nodes.rationale: A cost control rather than a safety one: the action already refuses bot actors, but only after paying for a ~508 MB checkout, and the review workflow's own comments quote @claude.

nodes.label: Job-level concurrency group
nodes.rationale: Declared on the job, not the workflow, because workflow-level concurrency is arbitrated before the if: is evaluated, so ordinary comments would join the group and evict a queued real request.

nodes.label: cancel-in-progress deliberately false
nodes.rationale: Claude can be mid-edit, mid-commit or mid-push when the next comment arrives; spend is capped with timeout-minutes instead.

nodes.label: issues.assigned deliberately not subscribed
nodes.rationale: The job condition tests the issue body and title rather than the event action, so assigning an already-answered issue would duplicate the reply and another 508 MB checkout.
